sentences.zh: 陳書卷八

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 8
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 8

sentences.zh: 列傳第二

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Two
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Two

sentences.zh: 杜僧明 周文育子寶安 侯安都

translations.literal: Du Sengming; Zhou Wenyu, son Bao'an; Hou Andu
translations.idiomatic: Du Sengming; Zhou Wenyu, son Bao'an; Hou Andu

sentences.zh: 杜僧明字弘照，廣陵臨澤人也。

translations.literal: Du Sengming, style Hongzhao, was a native of Linze in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Du Sengming, styled Hongzhao, came from Linze in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 形荞眇小，而膽氣過人，有勇力，善騎射。

translations.literal: Small in stature, yet his daring surpassed other men; he had courage and strength and was skilled in riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was small in stature, yet his daring surpassed other men; he had courage and strength and fought well from horseback.

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，盧安興為廣州南江督護，僧明與兄天合及周文育嵭為安興所啟，請與俱行。

translations.literal: In the Datong era of Liang, Lu Anxing was superintendent of the Southern River in Guangzhou; Sengming, his elder brother Tianhe, and Zhou Wenyu were all recommended by Anxing and asked to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's Datong era Lu Anxing was superintendent of Guangzhou's Southern River. Sengming, his elder brother Tianhe, and Zhou Wenyu were all brought forward by Anxing and went with him.

sentences.zh: 頻征俚獠有功，為新州助防。

translations.literal: He repeatedly campaigned against the Li and Liao with merit and was made assistant defender of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On repeated campaigns against the Li and Liao he earned merit and was made assistant defender of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 天合亦有材幹，預在征伐。

translations.literal: Tianhe also had ability and took part in the campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe too had talent and shared in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 安興死，僧明復副其子子雄。

translations.literal: When Anxing died, Sengming again served as deputy to his son Zixiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Anxing died, Sengming again served under his son Zixiong.

sentences.zh: 及交州土豪李賁反，逐刺史蕭諮，諮奔廣州，臺遣子雄與高州刺史孫冏討賁。

translations.literal: When the powerful local man Li Ben of Jiaozhou rebelled, drove out Inspector Xiao Zi, and Zi fled to Guangzhou, the court sent Zixiong and Sun Tong, inspector of Gaozhou, to campaign against Ben.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ben, a powerful man of Jiaozhou, rebelled and drove out Inspector Xiao Zi, who fled to Guangzhou, the court sent Zixiong and Sun Tong of Gaozhou against him.

sentences.zh: 時春草已生，瘴癘方起，子雄請待秋討之，廣州刺史新渝侯蕭谟不聽，蕭諮又促之，子雄等不得已，遂行。

translations.literal: Spring grass was already growing and miasma rising; Zixiong asked to wait until autumn to attack, but Xiao Mo, Prince of Xinyu and inspector of Guangzhou, would not listen, and Xiao Zi again pressed them, so Zixiong and the others had no choice but to march.
translations.idiomatic: Spring grass was up and miasma rising. Zixiong asked to wait for autumn, but Prince Xinyu Xiao Mo, inspector of Guangzhou, refused, and Xiao Zi pressed again, so they marched against their will.

sentences.zh: 至合浦，死者十六七，红嵭憚役潰散，禁之不可，乃引其餘兵退還。

translations.literal: Reaching Hepu, six or seven in ten died; the troops feared the corvée and scattered; they could not be stopped, and he led the remnant back.
translations.idiomatic: At Hepu six or seven in ten died. The troops feared the levy and broke; nothing could hold them, and he led the remnant home.

sentences.zh: 蕭諮啟子雄及冏與賊交通，逗留不進，梁武帝队於廣州賜死。

translations.literal: Xiao Zi reported that Zixiong and Tong had dealings with the bandits and lingered without advancing; Emperor Wu of Liang had them imprisoned at Guangzhou and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zi reported that Zixiong and Tong trafficked with the rebels and would not advance. Emperor Wu of Liang had them imprisoned at Guangzhou and put to death.

sentences.zh: 子雄弟子略、子烈嵭雄豪任俠，家屬在南江。

translations.literal: Zixiong's younger cousin Zilue and Zilie were bold and chivalrous; their families were in the Southern River region.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong's cousins Zilue and Zilie were bold and chivalrous men; their kin still lived in the Southern River country.

sentences.zh: 天合謀於红曰：「盧公累代待遇我等亦甚厚矣，今見枉而死，不能為報，非丈夫也。

translations.literal: Tianhe plotted with the troops, saying: "Master Lu treated us generously for generations; now he has been killed unjustly and we cannot repay him—this is not the act of a true man.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe took counsel with the troops: "The Lu house treated us well for generations; now they have been killed unjustly and we cannot repay them—what man would bear this?

sentences.zh: 我弟僧明萬人之敵，若圍州城，召百姓，誰敢不從。

translations.literal: My brother Sengming is a match for ten thousand men; if we surround the prefectural city and summon the people, who would not follow?
translations.idiomatic: My brother Sengming is worth ten thousand men. Ring the prefectural city and call the people—who would not answer?

sentences.zh: 城破，斬二侯祭孫、盧，然後待臺使至，束手詣廷尉，死猶勝生。

translations.literal: When the city falls, behead the two marquises to avenge Sun and Lu, then wait for the court envoy, bind our hands, and go to the Minister of Justice—death is better than life.
translations.idiomatic: When the walls fall, strike off the two marquises for Sun and Lu, then wait for the court envoy, go bound to the Minister of Justice, and die rather than live on in shame.

sentences.zh: 縱其不捷，亦無恨矣。

translations.literal: Even if we do not succeed, we shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Even if we fail, we shall have no regret."

sentences.zh: 」红咸慷慨曰「是願也，唯足下命之」。

translations.literal: The troops all cried out in zeal: "That is our wish; we await only your command."
translations.idiomatic: The troops answered hotly: "That is our wish; command us as you will."

sentences.zh: 乃與周文育等率红結盟，奉子雄弟子略為主，以攻刺史蕭映。

translations.literal: Thereupon, with Zhou Wenyu and others, he led the troops in alliance, set up Zixiong's cousin Zilue as leader, and attacked Inspector Xiao Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Then he and Zhou Wenyu and others swore the troops together, set up Zilue, Zixiong's cousin, as leader, and marched on Inspector Xiao Ying.

sentences.zh: 子略頓城南，天合頓城北，僧明、文育分據東西，吏人嵭應之，一日之中，红至數萬。

translations.literal: Zilue held the south of the city, Tianhe the north; Sengming and Wenyu held east and west; officials and people all responded; within a day troops reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zilue held the south gate, Tianhe the north; Sengming and Wenyu took east and west. Officials and commoners rose with them, and in a single day troops numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 高祖時在高要，聞事起，率红來討，大破之，殺天合，生擒僧明及文育等，高祖嵭釋之，引為主帥。

translations.literal: The Founder was then at Gaoyao; hearing of the rising, he led troops to attack, routed them utterly, killed Tianhe, and took Sengming and Wenyu alive; the Founder released them and made them his commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was at Gaoyao. Hearing of the revolt, he marched, broke them completely, killed Tianhe, and took Sengming and Wenyu alive. He freed them and kept them as his commanders.

sentences.zh: 高祖征交阯及討元景仲，僧明、文育嵭有功。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned in Jiaozhi and against Yuan Jingzhong, Sengming and Wenyu both had merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the Founder's campaigns in Jiaozhi and against Yuan Jingzhong, Sengming and Wenyu both won honor.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，俱隨高祖入援京師。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion they both followed the Founder to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion they both followed the Founder to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖於始興破蘭裕，僧明為前鋒，擒裕斬之。

translations.literal: When the Founder defeated Lan Yu at Shixing, Sengming was vanguard, took Yu prisoner, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder broke Lan Yu at Shixing, Sengming led the van, seized Yu, and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 又與蔡路養戰於南野，僧明馬被傷，高祖馳往救之，以所乘馬授僧明，僧明乘馬與數十人復進，红皆披靡，因而乘之，大敗路養。

translations.literal: Again, fighting Cai Luyang at Nanye, Sengming's horse was wounded; the Founder galloped to save him and gave him his own mount; Sengming remounted and with several dozen men pressed on again; the troops all scattered before him, and pressing the advantage he routed Luyang utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting Cai Luyang at Nanye, Sengming's horse was wounded. The Founder galloped to his aid and gave him his own mount. Sengming charged again with a few dozen men; the troops broke before him, and he drove Luyang to utter defeat.

sentences.zh: 高州刺史李遷仕又據大奛，入灨石，以逼高祖，高祖遣周文育為前軍，與僧明擊走之。

translations.literal: Li Qianshi, inspector of Gaozhou, again held Daqiang, entered Ganshi, and pressed the Founder; the Founder sent Zhou Wenyu as vanguard with Sengming to drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi of Gaozhou again held Daqiang, entered Ganshi, and threatened the Founder. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyu ahead with Sengming and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 遷仕與寧都人劉孝尚併力將襲南康，高祖又令僧明與文育等拒之，相持連戰百餘日，卒擒遷仕，送于高祖軍。

translations.literal: Qianshi and Liu Xiaoshang of Ningdu joined forces to strike at Nankang; the Founder again ordered Sengming with Wenyu and others to resist; they fought for more than a hundred days straight and at last took Qianshi and sent him to the Founder's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshi and Liu Xiaoshang of Ningdu meant to strike Nankang together. The Founder sent Sengming and Wenyu to hold them; for more than a hundred days they fought without rest, took Qianshi at last, and sent him to the Founder's camp.

sentences.zh: 及高祖下南康，留僧明頓西昌，督安成、廬陵二郡軍事。

translations.literal: When the Founder descended on Nankang he left Sengming at Xichang to oversee military affairs in Ancheng and Luling commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took Nankang he left Sengming at Xichang to command Ancheng and Luling.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制授假節、清野將軍、新州刺史，臨江縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, acting on provisional authority, granted him credential staff, general who clears the wilds, inspector of Xinzhou, and enfeoffment as Viscount of Linjiang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang, on provisional commission, made him credential-bearer, general who clears the wilds, inspector of Xinzhou, and Viscount of Linjiang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 周文育字景德，義興陽羨人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Wenyu, style Jingde, was a native of Yangxian in Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyu, styled Jingde, came from Yangxian in Yixing.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，本居新安壽昌縣，姓項氏，名猛奴。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he originally lived in Shouchang county in Xin'an; his surname was Xiang and his name Mengnu.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he had lived in Shouchang in Xin'an; his family name was Xiang and his childhood name Mengnu.

sentences.zh: 年十一，能反覆游水中數里，跳高五六尺，與戝兒聚戲，红莫能及。

translations.literal: At eleven he could swim back and forth in the water for several li and leap five or six chi; playing with village boys, none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he could swim several li back and forth and leap five or six chi high. Among village boys at play, none could match him.

sentences.zh: 義興人周薈為壽昌浦口戍主，見而奇之，因召與語。

translations.literal: Zhou Hui of Yixing was garrison chief at Shouchang Ford; seeing him, he marveled and summoned him to talk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hui of Yixing held the ford at Shouchang. Struck by the boy, he called him to speak.

sentences.zh: 文育對曰：「母老家貧，兄姊並長大，困於賦役。

translations.literal: Wenyu answered: "My mother is old, our house is poor, my elder brother and sisters are all grown, and we are crushed by taxes and corvée."
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu said, "Mother is old, the house is poor, brother and sisters are grown, and taxes and corvée crush us."

sentences.zh: 」薈哀之，乃隨文育至家，就其母請文育養為己子，母遂與之。

translations.literal: Hui pitied him, followed Wenyu home, and asked his mother to let him adopt Wenyu as his son; the mother consented.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was moved, went to his home, and asked his mother to let him adopt the boy; she agreed.

sentences.zh: 及薈秩滿，與文育還都，見於太子詹事周捨，請製名字，捨因為立名文育，字景德。

translations.literal: When Hui's term ended he returned to the capital with Wenyu, saw Zhou She, director of the heir apparent's household, and asked that a formal name be given; She thereupon named him Wenyu, style Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui's term ended he took Wenyu to the capital, saw Zhou She of the heir's household, and asked a formal name. She named him Wenyu and styled him Jingde.

sentences.zh: 命兄子弘讓教之書計。

translations.literal: He ordered his nephew Hongrang to teach him writing and reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He set his nephew Hongrang to teach him letters and accounts.

sentences.zh: 弘讓善隸書，寫蔡邕勸學及古詩以遺文育，文育不之省也，謂弘讓曰：「誰能學此，取富貴但有大槊耳。

translations.literal: Hongrang was skilled in clerical script and copied Cai Yong's Exhortation to Learning and ancient poems to give Wenyu; Wenyu did not look at them and said to Hongrang: "Who can learn this? To win wealth and rank you need only a great spear."
translations.idiomatic: Hongrang wrote clerical script well and copied Cai Yong's Exhortation to Learning and old poems for him. Wenyu never read them and told Hongrang, "Who learns such things? Wealth and rank come from a great spear alone."

sentences.zh: 」弘讓壯之，教之騎射，文育大悅。

translations.literal: Hongrang admired him and taught him riding and archery; Wenyu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hongrang admired his spirit and taught him riding and archery; Wenyu rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史陳慶之與薈同郡，素相善，啟薈為前軍軍主。

translations.literal: Inspector of Sizhou Chen Qingzhi was from the same commandery as Hui and on good terms with him; he recommended Hui as commander of the vanguard army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi, inspector of Sizhou, was Hui's countryman and friend and had him made commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 慶之使薈將五百人往新蔡懸瓠，慰勞白水蠻，蠻謀執薈以入魏，事覺，薈與文育拒之。

translations.literal: Qingzhi sent Hui with five hundred men to Xincai and Xuanhuo to comfort the White Water Man; the Man plotted to seize Hui and deliver him to Wei; the plot was discovered, and Hui with Wenyu resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi sent Hui with five hundred men to Xincai and Xuanhuo to comfort the White Water Man. The Man plotted to seize Hui for Wei; the plot came out, and Hui and Wenyu fought them off.

sentences.zh: 時賊徒甚盛，一日之中戰數十合，文育前鋒陷陣，勇冠軍中。

translations.literal: The bandits were very strong; in one day they fought several dozen engagements; Wenyu led the van and broke the line, his courage foremost in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were fierce; in a single day they fought dozens of times. Wenyu led the van and broke the array, bravest in the host.

sentences.zh: 薈於陣戰死，文育馳取其尸，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Hui died in battle; Wenyu galloped to take his corpse, and the bandits did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fell on the field. Wenyu galloped in for his body, and the rebels did not dare close.

sentences.zh: 及夕，各引去。

translations.literal: By evening each side withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At evening both sides drew off.

sentences.zh: 文育身被九創，創愈，辭請還葬，慶之壯其節，厚加賵遺而遣之。

translations.literal: Wenyu bore nine wounds; when they healed he asked leave to bury Hui; Qingzhi admired his constancy, gave him rich gifts, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu took nine wounds. When they healed he begged leave to bury Hui. Qingzhi honored his loyalty, gave him rich gifts, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 葬訖，會盧安興為南江督護，啟文育同行。

translations.literal: After the burial Lu Anxing became superintendent of the Southern River and recommended Wenyu to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites Lu Anxing became superintendent of the Southern River and had Wenyu go with him.

sentences.zh: 累征俚獠，所在有功，除南海令。

translations.literal: On repeated campaigns against the Li and Liao he had merit wherever he went and was made magistrate of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: On repeated campaigns against the Li and Liao he won merit everywhere and was made magistrate of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 安興死後，文育與杜僧明攻廣州，為高祖所敗，高祖赦之，語在僧明傳。

translations.literal: After Anxing's death Wenyu with Du Sengming attacked Guangzhou, was defeated by the Founder, and the Founder pardoned him—the account is in Sengming's biography.
translations.idiomatic: After Anxing died Wenyu and Du Sengming attacked Guangzhou, were beaten by the Founder, and pardoned—the tale is told in Sengming's biography.

sentences.zh: 後監州王勱以文育為長流

translations.literal: Later Supervisor of the Province Wang Li made Wenyu chief
translations.idiomatic: Later Supervisor Wang Li made Wenyu chief

translations.literal: (magistrate)
translations.idiomatic: (magistrate)

sentences.zh: ，[3]深被委任。

translations.literal: , Editorial footnote marker 3. and deeply trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: [3] and trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 勱被代，文育欲與勱俱下，至大庾嶺，詣卜者，卜者曰：「君北下不過作令長，南入則為公侯。

translations.literal: When Li was replaced Wenyu wished to go downriver with him; reaching Dayu Ridge he consulted a diviner, who said: "If you go north you will be no more than a magistrate; if you go south you will become a marquis or duke."
translations.idiomatic: When Li was replaced Wenyu meant to go down with him. At Dayu Ridge he asked a diviner, who said, "Go north and you will be no more than a magistrate; go south and you will be marquis or duke."

sentences.zh: 」文育曰：「足錢便可，誰望公侯。

translations.literal: Wenyu said: "Enough money is enough—who looks to be marquis or duke?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu said, "Enough silver is enough—who dreams of marquis or duke?"

sentences.zh: 」卜人又曰：「君須臾當暴得銀至二千兩，若不見信，以此為驗。

translations.literal: The diviner also said: "You will presently gain two thousand taels of silver at a stroke; if you do not believe it, take this as proof."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner added, "You will soon win two thousand taels of silver at a throw. If you doubt it, watch for this sign."

sentences.zh: 」其夕，宿逆旅，有賈人求與文育博，文育勝之，得銀二千兩。

translations.literal: That evening he lodged at an inn; a merchant asked to gamble with Wenyu; Wenyu won and took two thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: That night at an inn a merchant asked to gamble. Wenyu won two thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 旦日辭勱，勱問其故，文育以告，勱乃遣之。

translations.literal: Next morning he took leave of Li; Li asked the reason; Wenyu told him, and Li then sent him on.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he bade Li farewell. Li asked why; Wenyu told him, and Li sent him south.

sentences.zh: 高祖在高要，聞其還也，大喜，遣人迎之，厚加賞賜，分麾下配焉。

translations.literal: The Founder was at Gaoyao; hearing of his return he was greatly pleased, sent men to welcome him, rewarded him richly, and assigned men from his own command.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was at Gaoyao. Hearing Wenyu had returned, he rejoiced, sent men to meet him, gave rich rewards, and allotted troops from his own command.

sentences.zh: 高祖之討侯景，文育與杜僧明為前軍，克蘭裕，援歐陽頠，皆有功。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Hou Jing, Wenyu with Du Sengming were vanguard, took Lan Yu, relieved Ouyang Yi, and in each had merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the Founder's campaign against Hou Jing, Wenyu and Du Sengming led the van, took Lan Yu, relieved Ouyang Yi, and won merit in every fight.

sentences.zh: 高祖破蔡路養於南野，文育為路養所圍，四面數重，矢石雨下，所乘馬死，文育右手搏戰，左手解鞍，潰圍而出，因與杜僧明等相得，並力復進，遂大敗之。

translations.literal: When the Founder broke Cai Luyang at Nanye, Wenyu was surrounded by Luyang, several rings deep on every side, arrows and stones raining; his horse died; Wenyu fought with his right hand and with his left unbuckled the saddle, broke out of the encirclement, joined Du Sengming and the others, joined strength again, and at last routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder broke Cai Luyang at Nanye, Wenyu was ringed by Luyang, arrows and stones like rain, his horse killed. He fought with his right hand, unbuckled the saddle with his left, burst the ring, found Sengming and the rest, charged again together, and routed Luyang utterly.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃表文育為府司馬。

translations.literal: The Founder then memorialized that Wenyu be made staff marshal of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder then had Wenyu made staff marshal of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 李遷仕之據大夹，遣其將杜平虜入灨石魚梁作城，高祖命文育擊之，平虜棄城走，文育據其城。

translations.literal: When Li Qianshi held Daqiang he sent his general Du Pinglu into Ganshi to build a fort at Yuliang; the Founder ordered Wenyu to attack; Pinglu abandoned the fort and fled, and Wenyu took it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi held Daqiang and sent Du Pinglu into Ganshi to build at Yuliang. The Founder ordered Wenyu against him. Pinglu fled the fort and Wenyu seized it.

sentences.zh: 遷仕聞平虜敗，留老弱於大夹，悉選精兵自將，以攻文育，其鋒甚銳，軍人憚之。

translations.literal: Qianshi heard Pinglu had been beaten, left the old and weak at Daqiang, chose picked troops to lead himself, and attacked Wenyu; his edge was very sharp and the soldiers feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Pinglu was beaten, Qianshi left the weak at Daqiang, chose elite troops, and led them against Wenyu himself. His spear was sharp and the army feared him.

sentences.zh: 文育與戰，遷仕稍劔，相持未解，會高祖遣杜僧明來援，別破遷仕水軍，遷仕红潰，不敢過大夹，直走新淦。

translations.literal: Wenyu fought him; Qianshi gradually gave ground; the stalemate was not broken; the Founder sent Du Sengming to aid him; he separately broke Qianshi's river army; Qianshi's troops collapsed; he did not dare pass Daqiang and fled straight to Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu met him in battle. Qianshi slowly gave way; the fight hung deadlocked until the Founder sent Du Sengming. Sengming broke Qianshi's fleet apart; Qianshi's troops collapsed, he dared not pass Daqiang, and fled to Xingan.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝授文育假節、雄信將軍、義州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang granted Wenyu credential staff, stern-faith general, and inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang gave Wenyu credential staff, stern-faith general, and inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷仕又與劉孝尚謀拒義軍，高祖遣文育與侯安都、杜僧明、徐度、杜稜築城於白口拒之。

translations.literal: Qianshi again plotted with Liu Xiaoshang to resist the army of righteousness; the Founder sent Wenyu with Hou Andu, Du Sengming, Xu Du, and Du Ling to build a fort at Baikou to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshi again joined Liu Xiaoshang to resist the loyal army. The Founder sent Wenyu with Hou Andu, Du Sengming, Xu Du, and Du Ling to fortify Baikou.

sentences.zh: 文育頻出與戰，遂擒遷仕。

translations.literal: Wenyu went out repeatedly to fight and at last took Qianshi prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu sallied again and again and at last took Qianshi.

sentences.zh: 高祖發自南康，遣文育將兵五千，開通江路。

translations.literal: The Founder set out from Nankang and sent Wenyu with five thousand men to open the Tong River route.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder marched from Nankang and sent Wenyu with five thousand men to open the Tong River road.

sentences.zh: 侯景將王伯醜據豫章，文育擊走之，遂據其城。

translations.literal: Hou Jing's general Wang Bichou held Yuzhang; Wenyu drove him off and then held the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's general Wang Bichou held Yuzhang. Wenyu drove him off and took the city.

sentences.zh: 累前後功，除游騎將軍、員外散騎常侍，封東遷縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was made general of roaming cavalry, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongqian with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated honors he was made general of roaming cavalry and supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and enfeoffed Marquis of Dongqian with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖軍至白茅灣，命文育與杜僧明常為軍鋒，平南陵、鵲頭諸城。

translations.literal: When the Founder's army reached Baimao Bay he ordered Wenyu and Du Sengming always to serve as army point; they pacified Nanling, Que tou, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: At Baimao Bay the Founder set Wenyu and Du Sengming always at the army's point and they took Nanling, Que tou, and other towns.

sentences.zh: 及至姑熟，與景將侯子鑒戰，破之。

translations.literal: Reaching Gushu he fought Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: At Gushu he fought Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian and broke him.

sentences.zh: 景平，授通直散騎常侍，改封南移縣侯，邑一千戶，拜信義太守。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified he was made direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, his enfeoffment changed to Marquis of Nanyi with a fief of one thousand households, and he was appointed administrator of Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell he was made direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, raised to Marquis of Nanyi with one thousand households, and made administrator of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 累遷南丹陽蘭陵晉陵太守、智武將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to administrator of Nandanyang, Lanling, and Jinling, wise martial general, and scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through administrator of Nandanyang, Lanling, and Jinling to wise-martial general and scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖誅王僧辯，命文育督红軍會世祖於吳興，圍杜龕，克之。

translations.literal: When the Founder executed Wang Sengbian he ordered Wenyu to command the army and join Emperor Wen at Wuxing to besiege Du Kan and take him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder killed Wang Sengbian he sent Wenyu to command troops and join Emperor Wen at Wuxing, besiege Du Kan, and take him.

sentences.zh: 又濟江襲會稽太守張彪，得其郡城。

translations.literal: He also crossed the river in a surprise attack on Kuaiji Administrator Zhang Biao and took the commandery city.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river in a surprise stroke on Zhang Biao, administrator of Kuaiji, and seized the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 及世祖為彪所襲，文育時頓城北香巖寺，世祖夜往趨之，因共立柵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was attacked by Biao, Wenyu was then encamped at Xiangyan Temple north of the city; Emperor Wen went by night to join him, and together they built a palisade.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao struck Emperor Wen, Wenyu lay at Xiangyan Temple north of the city. Emperor Wen came by night; together they threw up a palisade.

sentences.zh: 頃之，彪又來攻，文育悉力苦戰，彪不能克，遂破平彪。

translations.literal: Before long Biao attacked again; Wenyu fought with all his strength; Biao could not take him and was at last broken and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Biao attacked again. Wenyu fought with everything he had; Biao could not break him and was destroyed at last.

sentences.zh: 高祖以侯瑱擁據

translations.literal: The Founder, because Hou Tian held
translations.idiomatic: Because Hou Tian held

translations.literal: (Wen)
translations.idiomatic: (Wen)

sentences.zh: [江]州，[4]命文育討之，仍除都督南豫州諸軍

translations.literal: [Jiang] province, Editorial footnote marker 4. ordered Wenyu to campaign against him and at the same time made him commander-in-chief of the military affairs of South Yuzhou
translations.idiomatic: Jiang province [4], the Founder ordered Wenyu against him and made him commander-in-chief of South Yuzhou

translations.literal: (affairs)
translations.idiomatic: (affairs)

sentences.zh: 事、武威將軍、南豫州刺史，[5]率兵襲湓城。

translations.literal: , martial prestige general, and inspector of South Yuzhou, Editorial footnote marker 5. and led troops in a surprise attack on Xuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: [5], martial-prestige general and inspector of South Yuzhou, and sent him to storm Xuncheng.

sentences.zh: 未克，徐嗣徽引齊寇渡江據蕪湖，詔徵文育還京。

translations.literal: He did not take it; Xu Siwei brought Qi invaders across the river and held Wuhu; an edict recalled Wenyu to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xuncheng did not fall. Xu Siwei brought Qi troops across the Yangzi and held Wuhu; an edict recalled Wenyu to the capital.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽等列艦於青墩，至於七磯，以斷文育歸路。

translations.literal: Siwei and the others lined ships from Qingdun to Qiji to cut Wenyu's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Siwei ranged ships from Qingdun to Qiji to sever Wenyu's retreat.

sentences.zh: 及夕，文育鼓噪而發，嗣徽等不能制。

translations.literal: At evening Wenyu drummed and set out shouting; Siwei and the others could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Wenyu beat the drums and broke out shouting. Siwei could not hold him.

sentences.zh: 至旦，反攻嗣徽，嗣徽驍將鮑砰獨以小艦殿軍，文育乘單舴艋與戰，跳入艦，斬砰，仍牽其艦而還。

translations.literal: At dawn he turned and attacked Siwei; Siwei's fierce general Bao Peng alone with a small ship brought up the rear; Wenyu boarded a single skiff to fight, leaped into Peng's ship, beheaded Peng, and towed the ship back.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he turned on Siwei. Siwei's champion Bao Peng alone brought up the rear in a small craft. Wenyu took a single skiff, leaped aboard, killed Peng, and towed the ship away.

sentences.zh: 賊红大駭，因留船蕪湖，自丹陽步上。

translations.literal: The rebel troops were greatly shaken; they therefore left their ships at Wuhu and went up from Danyang on foot.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel host was shaken. They left their ships at Wuhu and marched up from Danyang on foot.

sentences.zh: 時高祖拒嗣徽於白城，適與文育大會。

translations.literal: The Founder was then resisting Siwei at Baicheng and happened to join Wenyu in great force.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was holding Siwei at Baicheng and met Wenyu in full strength.

sentences.zh: 將戰，風急，高祖曰：「兵不逆風。

translations.literal: About to give battle, the wind was fierce; the Founder said: "Troops do not go against the wind."
translations.idiomatic: As battle neared the wind blew hard. The Founder said, "Soldiers do not fight against the wind."

sentences.zh: 」[6]文育曰：「事急矣，當決之，何用古法。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 6. Wenyu said: "The matter is urgent—we must decide; what use is the old rule?"
translations.idiomatic: [6] Wenyu said, "This is urgent—we must decide now. What use is the old rule?"

sentences.zh: 」抽槊上馬，馳而進，[7]红軍從之，風亦尋轉，殺傷數百人。

translations.literal: He drew his spear, mounted, and galloped forward; Editorial footnote marker 7. the army followed; the wind soon shifted too, and several hundred were killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his spear, mounted, and charged. [7] The army followed; the wind shifted; several hundred fell killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽等移營莫府山，[8]文育徙頓對之。

translations.literal: Siwei and the others moved camp to Mofu Mountain; Editorial footnote marker 8. Wenyu shifted his encampment to face them.
translations.idiomatic: Siwei moved camp to Mofu Mountain. [8] Wenyu shifted to face him.

sentences.zh: 頻戰功最，加平西將軍，進爵壽昌縣公，並給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In repeated fighting his merit was foremost; he was advanced to general who pacifies the west and raised to Duke of Shouchang, and was also given one set of pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated fighting his merit stood first. He was made general who pacifies the west, raised to Duke of Shouchang, and given pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史蕭勃舉兵踰嶺，詔文育督红軍討之。

translations.literal: Xiao Bo, inspector of Guangzhou, raised troops and crossed the ranges; an edict ordered Wenyu to command the army to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bo, inspector of Guangzhou, rose and crossed the mountains. An edict set Wenyu at the head of the army against him.

sentences.zh: 時新吳洞主余孝頃

translations.literal: At that time the cave lord of Xinwu Yu Xiaoding
translations.idiomatic: Then Yu Xiaoding, cave lord of Xinwu,

translations.literal: (Feng)
translations.idiomatic: (Feng)

sentences.zh: [舉]兵應勃，[9]遣其弟孝勱守郡城，自出豫章，據于石頭。

translations.literal: [raised] troops in response to Bo, Editorial footnote marker 9. sent his younger brother Xiaoxun to hold the commandery city, and himself came out to Yuzhang and held Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: [9] rose for Bo, sent his brother Xiaoxun to hold the commandery seat, and himself marched to Yuzhang and seized Shitou.

sentences.zh: 勃使其子孜將兵與孝頃相會，又遣其別將歐陽頠頓軍苦竹灘，傅泰據眏口城，[10]以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Bo sent his son Zi with troops to join Xiaoding and also sent his separate general Ouyang Yi to encamp at Kuzhu Ford and Fu Tai to hold Yankou city, Editorial footnote marker 10. to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Bo sent his son Zi to join Xiaoding and his generals Ouyang Yi to Kuzhu Ford and Fu Tai to Yankou [10] to block the loyal army.

sentences.zh: 官軍船少，孝頃有舴艋三百艘、艦百餘乘在上牢，[11]文育遣軍主焦僧度、羊柬潛軍襲之，悉取而歸，仍於豫章立柵。

translations.literal: The government army had few ships; Xiaoding had three hundred skiffs and more than a hundred war vessels upstream at Shanglao; Editorial footnote marker 11. Wenyu sent commanders Jiao Songdu and Yang Jian with a hidden force to strike them, took them all, and still built a palisade at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal army had few ships. Xiaoding kept three hundred skiffs and more than a hundred war craft at Shanglao. [11] Wenyu sent Jiao Songdu and Yang Jian in secret, seized them all, and threw up a palisade at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 時官軍食盡，嵭欲退還，文育不許。

translations.literal: At that time the government army's food was exhausted and all wished to withdraw; Wenyu would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Government grain was gone and every man wanted to pull back. Wenyu would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 乃使人間行遺周迪書，約為兄弟，並陳利害。

translations.literal: He then sent a man by hidden paths with a letter to Zhou Di, proposing brotherhood and setting out gain and harm.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a man by hidden paths with a letter to Zhou Di, calling him brother and weighing gain against harm.

sentences.zh: 迪得書甚喜，許饋糧餉。

translations.literal: Di was greatly pleased on receiving the letter and promised to send grain.
translations.idiomatic: Di was delighted by the letter and promised grain.

sentences.zh: 於是文育分遣老小乘故船舫，沿流俱下，燒豫章郡所立柵，偽退。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wenyu sent the old and weak down the old boats along the stream together, burned the palisade the Yuzhang commandery had set up, and feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu then sent the old and weak downriver on the old boats, burned the Yuzhang palisade, and pretended to retreat.

sentences.zh: 孝頃望之，大喜，因不設備。

translations.literal: Xiaoding watched them and was greatly pleased and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoding saw them go and rejoiced, and set no guard.

sentences.zh: 文育由間道兼行，信宿達芊韶。

translations.literal: Wenyu by a bypath marched day and night; in two nights he reached Qianshao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu took a hidden road and marched day and night; in two nights he reached Qianshao.

sentences.zh: 芊韶上流則歐陽頠、蕭勃，下流則傅泰、余孝頃，文育據其中間，築城饗士，賊徒大駭。

translations.literal: Upstream at Qianshao were Ouyang Yi and Xiao Bo; downstream Fu Tai and Yu Xiaoding; Wenyu held the middle, built a fort, and feasted his soldiers; the rebels were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Above Qianshao stood Ouyang Yi and Xiao Bo; below, Fu Tai and Yu Xiaoding. Wenyu held the middle, walled his men, and feasted them. The rebels were shaken.

sentences.zh: 歐陽頠乃退入泥溪，作城自守。

translations.literal: Ouyang Yi then withdrew into Nixi, built a fort, and held himself there.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Yi drew into Nixi, walled himself, and held firm.

sentences.zh: 文育遣嚴威將軍周鐵武，[12]與長史陸山才襲頠，擒之。

translations.literal: Wenyu sent Stern Prestige General Zhou Tiewu, Editorial footnote marker 12. with Chief Clerk Lu Shancai to strike Yi and took him prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu sent Stern Prestige General Zhou Tiewu [12] and chief clerk Lu Shancai against Yi and took him.

sentences.zh: 於是盛陳兵甲，與頠乘舟而讌，以巡傅泰城下，因而攻泰，克之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he displayed arms in force, feasted with Yi on a boat, and cruised below Fu Tai's walls, then attacked Tai and took him.
translations.idiomatic: He arrayed his arms, feasted with Yi on the water, and cruised under Fu Tai's walls, then stormed Tai and took him.

sentences.zh: 蕭勃在南康聞之，红皆股慄，莫能自固。

translations.literal: Xiao Bo at Nankang heard of it; the troops all trembled in their thighs and none could hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Bo at Nankang heard the news. His troops' thighs shook; none could stand firm.

sentences.zh: 其將譚世遠斬勃欲降，為人所害。

translations.literal: His general Tan Shiyuan beheaded Bo intending to surrender but was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: His general Tan Shiyuan struck off Bo's head to yield and was himself killed.

sentences.zh: 世遠軍主夏侯明徹持勃首以降。

translations.literal: Shiyuan's commander Xia Hou Mingche brought Bo's head to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan's officer Xia Hou Mingche came in with Bo's head.

sentences.zh: 蕭孜、余孝頃猶據石頭，高祖遣侯安都助文育攻之，孜降文育，孝頃退走新吳，廣州平，文育還頓豫章。

translations.literal: Xiao Zi and Yu Xiaoding still held Shitou; the Founder sent Hou Andu to aid Wenyu in attacking them; Zi surrendered to Wenyu, Xiaoding fled to Xinwu, Guangzhou was pacified, and Wenyu returned to encamp at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zi and Yu Xiaoding still held Shitou. The Founder sent Hou Andu to help Wenyu. Zi yielded to Wenyu; Xiaoding fled to Xinwu; Guangzhou was pacified; Wenyu returned to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 以功授鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司、都督江廣衡交等州諸軍事、江州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was made general who garrisons the south, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, commander-in-chief of the military affairs of Jiang, Guang, Heng, Jiao, and other provinces, and inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made general who garrisons the south with a mansion equal to the three dukes, commander-in-chief over Jiang, Guang, Heng, Jiao, and other provinces, and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王琳擁據上流，詔命侯安都為西道都督，文育為南道都督，同會武昌。

translations.literal: Wang Lin held the upper reaches; an edict appointed Hou Andu western-route commander-in-chief and Wenyu southern-route commander-in-chief to meet at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin held the upper river. An edict made Hou Andu western commander and Wenyu southern commander to join at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 與王琳戰於沌口，為琳所執，後得逃歸，語在安都傳。

translations.literal: He fought Wang Lin at Dankou, was seized by Lin, and later escaped and returned—the account is in Andu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: At Dankou he fought Wang Lin, was taken, and later escaped—the tale is in Andu's biography.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、散騎常侍、鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司，壽昌縣公，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted credential staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, general who garrisons the south, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Duke of Shouchang, and one set of pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received credential staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, general who garrisons the south, opener equal to the three dukes, Duke of Shouchang, and pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 及周迪破余孝頃，孝頃子公颺、弟孝勱猶據舊柵，扇動南土，高祖復遣文育及周迪、黃法矴等討之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Di broke Yu Xiaoding, Xiaoding's son Gongyang and younger brother Xiaoxun still held the old palisades and stirred the southern lands; the Founder again sent Wenyu with Zhou Di, Huang Fading, and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di broke Yu Xiaoding, Gongyang and Xiaoxun still held the old forts and stirred the south. The Founder again sent Wenyu with Zhou Di and Huang Fading against them.

sentences.zh: 豫章內史熊曇朗亦率軍來會，红且萬人。

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang, interior administrator of Yuzhang, also led troops to join them; troops numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tanlang, interior administrator of Yuzhang, brought his host as well; troops neared ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 文育遣吳明徹為水軍，配周迪運糧，自率红軍入象牙江，城於金口。

translations.literal: Wenyu made Wu Mingche the river army, assigned Zhou Di to transport grain, and himself led the army into Xiangya River and walled at Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu set Wu Mingche over the fleet, Zhou Di over grain, and himself led the army up Xiangya River and fortified Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 公颺領五百人偽降，謀執文育，事覺，文育囚之，送于京師，以其部曲分隸红軍。

translations.literal: Gongyang led five hundred men in false surrender, plotting to seize Wenyu; the plot was discovered; Wenyu imprisoned him and sent him to the capital, and divided his followers among the army.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang came in with five hundred men in false surrender, meaning to seize Wenyu. The plot came out. Wenyu jailed him, sent him to the capital, and split his men among the loyal ranks.

sentences.zh: 乃捨舟為步軍，進據三陂。

translations.literal: He then abandoned the boats for foot soldiers and advanced to hold Sanpo.
translations.idiomatic: He left the boats for foot soldiers and advanced to Sanpo.

sentences.zh: 王琳遣將曹慶帥兵二千人以救孝勱，慶分遣主帥常红愛與文育相拒，自帥所領徑攻周迪、吳明徹軍。

translations.literal: Wang Lin sent his general Cao Qing with two thousand men to rescue Xiaoxun; Qing separately sent his commander Chang Ai to resist Wenyu and himself led his command straight against Zhou Di and Wu Mingche's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent Cao Qing with two thousand men to save Xiaoxun. Qing sent Chang Ai against Wenyu and led his own command straight at Zhou Di and Wu Mingche.

sentences.zh: 迪等敗績，文育退據金口。

translations.literal: Di and the others were beaten; Wenyu withdrew to hold Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Di and Mingche were beaten. Wenyu fell back to Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 熊曇朗因其失利，謀害文育，以應红愛。

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang, taking advantage of his setback, plotted to kill Wenyu to join Chang Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tanlang, seeing his loss, plotted to kill Wenyu and join Chang Ai.

sentences.zh: 文育監軍孫白象頗知其事，勸令先之。

translations.literal: Wenyu's supervising officer Sun Baixiang knew something of the matter and urged him to strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu's supervisor Sun Baixiang knew the plot and urged a first blow.

sentences.zh: 文育曰：「不可，我舊兵少，客軍多，若取曇朗，人人驚懼，亡立至矣，不如推心以撫之。

translations.literal: Wenyu said: "It cannot be done. My old soldiers are few and the guest armies many; if we seize Tanlang, every man will be terrified and destruction will come at once—it is better to treat him with open heart and reassure him."
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu said, "No. My veterans are few and allied troops many. Seize Tanlang and every man panics—ruin comes at once. Better win him with an open hand."

sentences.zh: 」初，周迪之敗也，棄船走，莫知所在，及得迪書，文育喜，栏示曇朗，曇朗害之於座，時年五十一。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhou Di had been beaten he abandoned his boats and fled, and no one knew where he was; when he received Di's letter Wenyu rejoiced and showed it to Tanlang; Tanlang killed him at the seat; he was fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di had been beaten he abandoned his boats and vanished. A letter from Di came; Wenyu rejoiced and showed Tanlang. Tanlang killed him at table. He was fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，即日舉哀，贈侍中、司空，諡曰忠愍。

translations.literal: When the Founder heard he mourned the same day, posthumously made him palace attendant and minister of works, and gave the posthumous title Loyal Lament.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder mourned the same day, posthumously made him palace attendant and minister of works, and titled him Loyal Lament.

sentences.zh: 初，文育之據三陂，有流星墜地，其聲如雷，地陷方一丈，中有碎炭數斗。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wenyu held Sanpo, a shooting star fell to earth with a sound like thunder; the ground sank one zhang square and held several dou of broken charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu held Sanpo a meteor fell with thunder. The earth sank a square zhang and held several dou of charred coal.

sentences.zh: 又軍市中忽聞小兒啼，一市嵭驚，聽之在土下，軍人掘得棺長三尺，文育惡之。

translations.literal: Again in the army market a child's cry was suddenly heard; the whole market was alarmed; listening, it was under the earth; soldiers dug and found a coffin three chi long; Wenyu hated the omen.
translations.idiomatic: In the army market a child seemed to cry under the ground. Soldiers dug up a coffin three chi long. Wenyu hated the sign.

sentences.zh: 俄而迪敗，文育見殺。

translations.literal: Before long Di was beaten and Wenyu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Di was beaten and Wenyu was slain.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，有詔配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng an edict ordered him to share offerings in the Founder's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 2 (561) an edict gave him shared sacrifice in the Founder's temple.

sentences.zh: 子寶安嗣。

translations.literal: His son Bao'an succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao'an succeeded.

sentences.zh: 文育本族兄景曜，因文育官至新安太守。

translations.literal: Wenyu's clansman Jingyao, through Wenyu, reached the post of administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu's kinsman Jingyao, through Wenyu's favor, became administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 寶安字安民。

translations.literal: Bao'an, style Anmin.
translations.idiomatic: Bao'an, styled Anmin.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，便習騎射，以貴公子驕蹇遊逸，好狗馬，樂馳騁，靡衣媮食。

translations.literal: In his teens he was already skilled in riding and archery; as a noble's son he was proud, dissolute, and fond of roaming; he loved dogs and horses, delighted in the gallop, dressed in splendor and ate in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: In his teens he rode and shot well. As a noble's son he was proud and wild, loved hounds and horses, dressed fine, and ate idle.

sentences.zh: 文育之為晉陵，以征討不遑之郡，令寶安監知郡事，尤聚惡少年，高祖患之。

translations.literal: When Wenyu was at Jinling, because campaigns left no leisure for the commandery he had Bao'an oversee commandery affairs; he especially gathered wicked youths; the Founder was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu held Jinling he left Bao'an to run the commandery while he fought, and the boy gathered rowdies. The Founder disliked it.

sentences.zh: 及文育西征敗績，縶於王琳，寶安便折節讀書，與士君子遊，綏御文育士卒，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: When Wenyu was beaten on the western campaign and held by Wang Lin, Bao'an at once reformed himself, read books, kept company with gentlemen, and pacified Wenyu's soldiers with great authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu was beaten west and held by Wang Lin, Bao'an turned sober, read books, kept gentlemen's company, and ruled Wenyu's soldiers with stern kindness.

sentences.zh: 除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry gentleman.

sentences.zh: 文育歸，復除貞威將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: When Wenyu returned he was again made steadfast-prestige general and administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu came home he was again made steadfast-prestige general and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 文育為熊曇朗所害，徵寶安還。

translations.literal: When Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang, Bao'an was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong Tanlang killed Wenyu, Bao'an was recalled.

sentences.zh: 起為猛烈將軍，領其舊兵，仍令南討。

translations.literal: He was raised to fierce martial general, given command of his father's old troops, and still ordered south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was made fierce-martial general, given his father's old troops, and sent south again.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，深器重之，寄以心膂，精卒利兵多配焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne he valued him deeply, entrusted him as a confidant, and gave him many picked soldiers and sharp weapons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne he prized him, kept him close, and gave him picked men and good arms.

sentences.zh: 及平王琳，頗有功。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified he had considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: In pacifying Wang Lin he won solid merit.

sentences.zh: 周迪之破熊曇朗，寶安南入，窮其餘燼。

translations.literal: When Zhou Di broke Xiong Tanlang, Bao'an marched south and hunted down the last embers.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di broke Xiong Tanlang, Bao'an marched south and stamped out the last embers.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，重除雄信將軍、吳興太守，襲封壽昌縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was again made stern-faith general and administrator of Wuxing and succeeded to the enfeoffment as Duke of Shouchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 2 (561) he was again stern-faith general and administrator of Wuxing and succeeded as Duke of Shouchang.

sentences.zh: 三年，征留異，為侯安都前軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he campaigned against Liu Yi and was Hou Andu's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he campaigned against Liu Yi as Hou Andu's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 異平，除給事黃門侍郎、纫尉卿。

translations.literal: When Yi was pacified he was made gentleman of the yellow gate and commandant of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi fell he was made gentleman of the yellow gate and commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，授持節、都督南徐州諸軍事、貞毅將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was granted credential staff, made commander-in-chief of the military affairs of South Xuzhou, steadfast-resolve general, and inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he received credential staff, command over South Xuzhou, steadfast-resolve general, and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵為左纫將軍，加信武將軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made left guard general and given the additional title faithful-martial general.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was made left guard general with the added title faithful-martial general.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官領纫尉卿，又進號仁威將軍。

translations.literal: Soon, retaining his former office, he also headed the guard commandant's office and was advanced in title to benevolent-prestige general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also headed the guard while keeping his rank, and was raised to benevolent-prestige general.

sentences.zh: 天康元年卒，時年二十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he died, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiankang year 1 (566) he died, aged twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、左纫將軍，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made palace attendant and left guard general, with the posthumous title Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was palace attendant and left guard general, titled Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 子买嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ke succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ke succeeded.

sentences.zh: 寶安卒後，买亦為偏將。

translations.literal: After Bao'an died Ke also served as a subordinate general.
translations.idiomatic: After Bao'an died Ke too served as a subordinate general.

sentences.zh: 征歐陽紇，平定淮南，嵭有功，封江安縣伯，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Ouyang He and pacifying Huainan he had merit, was enfeoffed as Earl of Jiang'an with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Ouyang He and in pacifying Huainan he won merit and was enfeoffed Earl of Jiang'an with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 歷晉陵、定遠二郡太守。

translations.literal: He served as administrator of Jinling and Dingyuan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was administrator of Jinling and Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 太建九年卒，時年二十四，贈電威將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taijian he died, aged twenty-four, and was posthumously made serene-prestige general.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 9 (581) he died, aged twenty-four, and was posthumously made serene-prestige general.

sentences.zh: 侯安都字成師，始興曲江人也。

translations.literal: Hou Andu, style Chengshi, was a native of Qujiang in Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu, styled Chengshi, came from Qujiang in Shixing.

sentences.zh: 世為郡著姓。

translations.literal: For generations his house was a leading clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his house was a leading clan in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 父文捍，[13]少仕州郡，以忠謹稱，安都貴後，官至光祿大夫、始興內史，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: His father Wenhan, Editorial footnote marker 13. in youth served in the province and commandery and was known for loyalty and care; after Andu rose high he reached the posts of grand master for the imperial insignia and interior administrator of Shixing, with salary of middle two thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenhan [13] served the province and commandery in youth and was known for loyalty. After Andu rose, Wenhan became grand master for the imperial insignia and interior administrator of Shixing at middle two-thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: 安都工隸書，能鼓琴，涉獵書傳，為五言詩，亦頗清靡，兼善騎射，為邑里雄豪。

translations.literal: Andu was skilled in clerical script, could play the zither, ranged through books and records, composed five-character poems that were also rather refined, and was besides skilled in riding and archery—a local hero.
translations.idiomatic: Andu wrote clerical script, played the zither, read widely, wrote five-character verse of some grace, rode and shot well, and was a hero in his district.

sentences.zh: 梁始興內史蕭子範辟為主簿。

translations.literal: Xiao Zifan, interior administrator of Shixing under Liang, summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang, Xiao Zifan, interior administrator of Shixing, took him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，招集兵甲，至三千人。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he gathered arms and armor to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he gathered arms for three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 高祖入援京邑，安都引兵從高祖，攻蔡路養，破李遷仕，克平侯景，嵭力戰有功。

translations.literal: When the Founder entered to relieve the capital region, Andu led troops to follow the Founder, attacked Cai Luyang, broke Li Qianshi, and in conquering and pacifying Hou Jing fought with all his strength and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched to relieve the capital, Andu followed with troops, struck Cai Luyang, broke Li Qianshi, and in crushing Hou Jing fought with all his might and won honor.

sentences.zh: 元帝授猛烈將軍、通直散騎常侍，富川縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan granted him fierce-martial general, direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and enfeoffment as Viscount of Fuchuan with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang made him fierce-martial general and direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and Viscount of Fuchuan with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 隨高祖鎮京口，除蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: He followed the Founder in garrison at Jingkou and was made administrator of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Founder to Jingkou and was made administrator of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 高祖謀襲王僧辯，諸將莫有知者，唯與安都定計，仍使安都率水軍自京口趨石頭，高祖自率馬步從江乘羅落會之。

translations.literal: When the Founder plotted to strike Wang Sengbian none of the generals knew; he alone settled the plan with Andu and still had Andu lead the river army from Jingkou toward Shitou while the Founder himself led horse and foot from Jiangcheng and Luoluo to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder plotted against Wang Sengbian no general knew but Andu. Andu led the river force from Jingkou on Shitou while the Founder came with horse and foot from Jiangcheng and Luoluo to meet him.

sentences.zh: 安都至石頭北，棄舟登岸，僧辯弗之覺也。

translations.literal: Andu reached the north of Shitou, abandoned his boats, and went ashore; Sengbian did not perceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Andu reached north Shitou, left his boats, and went ashore unseen by Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 石頭城北接崗阜，雉堞不甚危峻，安都被甲帶長刀，軍人捧之投於女垣內，红隨而入，進逼僧辯臥室。

translations.literal: Shitou's north adjoins hills; the parapet was not very steep; Andu wore armor and carried a long blade; soldiers lifted him and cast him over the inner parapet; troops followed within, pressed forward, and closed on Sengbian's sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: North Shitou runs into hills and the wall was low. Andu wore armor and a long blade; soldiers lifted him onto the inner parapet; troops poured in and pressed on Sengbian's chamber.

sentences.zh: 高祖大軍亦至，與僧辯戰于聽事前，安都自內閤出，腹背擊之，遂擒僧辯。

translations.literal: The Founder's great army also arrived and fought Sengbian before the audience hall; Andu came out from the inner quarters and struck front and rear; he took Sengbian prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder's host came up and fought Sengbian before the hall. Andu burst from the inner quarters and struck fore and aft. Sengbian was taken.

sentences.zh: 明年春，詔安都率兵鎮梁山，以備齊。

translations.literal: The next spring an edict ordered Andu to lead troops to garrison Liang Mountain against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring an edict set Andu to garrison Liang Mountain against Qi.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽等復入丹陽，[14]至湖熟，高祖追安都還，率馬步拒之於高橋。

translations.literal: Xu Siwei and others again entered Danyang, Editorial footnote marker 14. reaching Hushu; the Founder recalled Andu and led horse and foot to resist them at Gaoqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Siwei again entered Danyang [14] as far as Hushu. The Founder recalled Andu and met them at Gaoqiao with horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 又戰於耕壇南，安都率十二騎，突其陣，破之，生擒齊儀同乞伏無勞。

translations.literal: Again they fought south of Gengtan; Andu led twelve horsemen and burst their line, broke them, and took alive Qi Acting Minister of State Qifu Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again south of Gengtan. Andu with twelve riders burst the line, broke them, and took Qifu Wulao of Qi alive.

sentences.zh: 又刺齊將東方老墮馬，會賊騎至，救老獲免。

translations.literal: He also speared Qi general Dongfang Lao and knocked him from his horse; rebel horsemen came and rescued Lao, who escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He speared Qi general Dongfang Lao from the saddle; enemy riders came and Lao escaped.

sentences.zh: 賊北渡蔣山，安都又與齊將王敬寶戰於龍尾，使從弟曉、軍主張纂前犯其陣。

translations.literal: The bandits crossed north over Jiangshan; Andu again fought Qi general Wang Jingbao at Longwei and sent his cousin Xiao and commander Zhang Zuan to strike the front of their line.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed Jiangshan north. Andu fought Wang Jingbao of Qi at Longwei and sent his cousin Xiao and Zhang Zuan against the van.

sentences.zh: 曉被槍墜馬，張纂死之。

translations.literal: Xiao was speared and fell from his horse; Zhang Zuan died in the fight.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao took a spear and fell. Zhang Zuan died on the field.

sentences.zh: 安都馳往救曉，斬其騎士十一人，因取纂尸而還，齊軍不敢逼。

translations.literal: Andu galloped to save Xiao, beheaded eleven of their horsemen, took Zuan's corpse and returned, and the Qi army did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: Andu galloped to Xiao, killed eleven horsemen, bore Zuan's body back, and Qi did not dare follow.

sentences.zh: 高祖與齊軍戰於莫府山，命安都領步騎千餘人，自白下橫擊其後，齊軍大敗。

translations.literal: The Founder fought the Qi army at Mofu Mountain and ordered Andu to lead more than a thousand foot and horse from Baixia to strike them in the rear crosswise; the Qi army was routed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: At Mofu Mountain the Founder fought Qi and sent Andu with more than a thousand horse and foot from Baixia to strike their rear. Qi broke utterly.

sentences.zh: [15]安都又率所部追至攝山，俘獲首虜，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 15. Andu again led his command in pursuit to She Mountain, capturing heads and prisoners beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: [15] Andu pursued to She Mountain and took heads and prisoners past counting.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為侯，增邑五百戶，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced in enfeoffment to marquis, his fief increased by five hundred households, and he was given one set of pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: For merit his fief was raised to marquis with five hundred added households and he received pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 又進號平南將軍，改封西江縣公。

translations.literal: He was again advanced in title to general who pacifies the south and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Xijiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to general who pacifies the south and made Duke of Xijiang.

sentences.zh: 仍都督水軍出豫章，助豫州刺史周文育討蕭勃。

translations.literal: He still commanded the river army out of Yuzhang to aid Inspector of Yuzhou Zhou Wenyu in campaigning against Xiao Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He still commanded the fleet from Yuzhang to aid Zhou Wenyu, inspector of Yuzhou, against Xiao Bo.

sentences.zh: 安都未至，文育已斬勃，並擒其將歐陽頠、傅泰等。

translations.literal: Andu had not yet arrived when Wenyu had already beheaded Bo and also taken his generals Ouyang Yi, Fu Tai, and others prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Before Andu arrived Wenyu had beheaded Bo and taken Ouyang Yi, Fu Tai, and others.

sentences.zh: 唯余孝頃與勃子孜猶據豫章之石頭，作兩城，孝頃與孜各據其一，又多設船艦，夾水而陣。

translations.literal: Only Yu Xiaoding and Bo's son Zi still held Shitou in Yuzhang, building two cities; Xiaoding and Zi each held one; they also set out many ships and boats and lined their battle line across the water.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yu Xiaoding and Bo's son Zi still held Shitou in Yuzhang in twin cities. They massed ships and lined the water with battle line.

sentences.zh: 安都至，乃銜枚夜燒其艦。

translations.literal: When Andu arrived he had men take sticks in their mouths by night and burn their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Andu came, had men gag themselves with sticks at night, and burned their fleet.

sentences.zh: 文育率水軍，安都領步騎，登岸結陣。

translations.literal: Wenyu led the river army; Andu led foot and horse; they went ashore and formed battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu led the fleet; Andu the foot and horse. They landed and formed line.

sentences.zh: 孝頃俄斷後路，安都乃令軍士多伐松木，嵳柵，列營漸進，頻戰屢克，孜乃降。

translations.literal: Xiaoding soon cut off the rear road; Andu then ordered the soldiers to cut much pine wood, pile palisades, advance camp by camp, fought repeatedly and won repeatedly, and Zi then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoding cut the retreat. Andu had pine felled, palisades raised, camps pushed forward, won fight after fight, and Zi yielded.

sentences.zh: 孝頃奔歸新吳，請入子為質，許之。

translations.literal: Xiaoding fled back to Xinwu and asked to send his son as hostage; this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoding fled to Xinwu and offered his son as hostage; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 師還，以功進號鎮北將軍，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for merit he was advanced in title to general who garrisons the north and given opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was raised to general who garrisons the north and opener equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 仍率红會於武昌，與周文育西討王琳。

translations.literal: He still led the army to join at Wuchang with Zhou Wenyu in the western campaign against Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He still led troops to Wuchang to join Zhou Wenyu against Wang Lin in the west.

sentences.zh: 將發，王公已下餞於新林，安都躍馬渡橋，人馬俱墮水中，又坐湾內墜於櫓井，時以為不祥。

translations.literal: As they were about to set out, from the nobles down they saw them off at Xinlin; Andu leaped his horse over a bridge, man and horse both falling into the water; again, sitting in a skiff he fell into the sculling-well in the cabin—at the time it was thought ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinlin nobles saw them off. Andu leaped a bridge and horse and rider plunged into the water; in a skiff he fell into the sculling-well—omens of ill luck.

sentences.zh: 至武昌，琳將樊猛棄城走。

translations.literal: Reaching Wuchang, Wang Lin's general Fan Meng abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuchang Wang Lin's general Fan Meng abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 文育亦自豫章至。

translations.literal: Wenyu also came from Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu too came from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 時兩將俱行，不相統攝，因部下交爭，稍不平。

translations.literal: At that time both generals marched together without unified command; because their subordinates quarreled they grew somewhat estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Both generals marched without one command. Their men quarreled and the two grew cool.

sentences.zh: 軍至郢州，琳將潘純鲶於城中遙射官軍，[16]安都怒，進軍圍之，未能克。

translations.literal: The army reached Yingzhou; Wang Lin's general Pan Chunzhi shot at the government army from the city from afar; Editorial footnote marker 16. Andu was enraged, advanced and besieged the city, but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingzhou Wang Lin's general Pan Chunzhi shot from the walls. [16] Andu raged, besieged the city, and could not take it.

sentences.zh: 而王琳至于弇口，安都乃釋郢州，悉红往沌口以禦之，遇風不得進。

translations.literal: Wang Lin then reached Yan mouth; Andu released Yingzhou and led all the troops to Dankou to meet him but met wind and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin reached Yan mouth. Andu left Yingzhou, marched every man to Dankou, and was stopped by wind.

sentences.zh: 琳據東岸，官軍據西岸，相持數日，乃合戰，安都等敗績。

translations.literal: Lin held the east bank and the government army the west; they faced each other several days, then joined battle; Andu and the others were beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Lin held the east bank, the loyal army the west. After days they fought. Andu and the rest were beaten.

sentences.zh: 安都與周文育、徐敬成並為琳所囚。

translations.literal: Andu, Zhou Wenyu, and Xu Jingcheng were alike imprisoned by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyu, and Xu Jingcheng were all imprisoned by Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 琳總以一長鎖繫之，置于湾下，令所親宦者王子晉掌視之。

translations.literal: Lin always bound them with one long chain and placed them under the boat shelter, ordering his close eunuch Wang Zijin to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin always bound them with one long chain and kept them under the boats, putting his trusted eunuch Wang Zijin in charge of watching them.

sentences.zh: 琳下至湓城白水浦，安都等甘言許厚賂子晉。

translations.literal: When Lin descended to White Water Ford at Pencheng, Andu and the rest with sweet words promised Zijin great bribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin went down to White Water Ford at Pencheng, Andu and the others flattered Zijin and promised him rich bribes.

sentences.zh: 子晉乃偽以小船依湾而釣，夜載安都、文育、敬成上岸，入深草中，步投官軍。

translations.literal: Zijin then feigned fishing in a small boat by the shelter; at night he carried Andu, Wenyu, and Jingcheng ashore into deep grass, and on foot they fled to the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Zijin then pretended to fish from a small boat moored by the shelter; at night he ferried Andu, Wenyu, and Jingcheng ashore into deep grass, and they made their way on foot to the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 還都自劾，詔嵭赦之，復其官爵。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he impeached himself; an edict specially pardoned him and restored his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he submitted a confession; an edict granted him special pardon and restored his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 尋為丹陽尹，出為都督南豫州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Intendant of Danyang, then sent out as Director-General of all military affairs in Southern Yuzhou, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became intendant of Danyang, then was sent out as director-general of all military affairs in Southern Yuzhou, general who pacifies the west, and Southern Yuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 令繼周文育攻余孝勱及王琳將曹慶、常红愛等。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow Zhou Wenyu in attacking Yu Xiaomo and Wang Lin's generals Cao Qing, Chang Hong'ai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to follow Zhou Wenyu against Yu Xiaomo and Wang Lin's generals Cao Qing, Chang Hong'ai, and others.

sentences.zh: 安都自宮亭湖出松門，躡红愛後。

translations.literal: Andu left from Gongting Lake through Song Gate and tracked Hong'ai's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Andu left Gongting Lake by Song Gate and pressed on Hong'ai's rear.

sentences.zh: 文育為熊曇朗所害，安都回取大艦，值琳將周炅、周協南歸，與戰，破之，生擒炅、協。

translations.literal: Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Andu turned back to take great ships and happened on Lin's generals Zhou Jiong and Zhou Xie returning south; he fought, defeated them, and captured Jiong and Xie alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Andu turned back for large ships, met Lin's generals Zhou Jiong and Zhou Xie heading south, defeated them, and took Jiong and Xie alive.

sentences.zh: 孝勱弟孝猷率部下四千家欲就王琳，遇炅、協敗，乃詣安都降。

translations.literal: Xiaomo's younger brother Xiaoyou led four thousand households of his following intending to join Wang Lin; encountering Jiong and Xie's defeat, he thereupon came to Andu and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaomo's brother Xiaoyou led four thousand households toward Wang Lin; when Jiong and Xie were beaten, he came to Andu and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 安都又進軍於禽奇洲，破曹慶、常红愛等，焚其船艦。

translations.literal: Andu again advanced to Qinqi Isle, defeated Cao Qing, Chang Hong'ai, and the rest, and burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Andu advanced again to Qinqi Isle, routed Cao Qing, Chang Hong'ai, and the rest, and burned their fleet.

sentences.zh: 红愛奔于廬山，為村人所殺，餘红悉平。

translations.literal: Hong'ai fled to Mount Lu and was killed by villagers; the remaining Hong factions were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hong'ai fled to Mount Lu, where villagers killed him; the rest of the Hong faction was pacified.

sentences.zh: 還軍至南皖，而高祖崩，安都隨世祖還朝，仍與戝臣定議，翼奉世祖。

translations.literal: Returning the army to Southern Wan, the Founder died; Andu followed Emperor Wen back to court and still joined the great ministers in settling plans to aid and install Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: On the march back to Southern Wan the Founder died; Andu followed Emperor Wen to court and joined the great ministers in settling the succession and supporting him.

sentences.zh: 時世祖謙讓弗敢當，太后又以衡陽王故，未肯下令，戝臣猶豫不能決。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wen modestly declined and dared not accept; the empress dowager also because of the Prince of Hengyang would not issue the order; the great ministers hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen modestly refused the throne; the empress dowager, mindful of the Prince of Hengyang, would not issue the order; the ministers wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 安都曰：「今四方未定，何暇及遠，臨川王有功天下，須共立之。

translations.literal: Andu said: "Now the four directions are unsettled—who has leisure for distant concerns? The Prince of Linchuan has merit under heaven; we must together install him.
translations.idiomatic: Andu said: "The realm is still unsettled—who has time for distant claims? The Prince of Linchuan has served the realm; we must enthrone him together.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，後應者斬。

translations.literal: In today's matter, whoever responds afterward is to be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever hesitates today will be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 」便按闰上殿，白太后出璽，又手解世祖髮，推就喪次。

translations.literal: He then pressed up to the hall, told the empress dowager to bring out the seal, and with his own hands loosened Emperor Wen's hair and pushed him toward the mourning place.
translations.idiomatic: He then escorted him into the hall, had the empress dowager produce the seal, loosened Emperor Wen's mourning hair with his own hands, and pushed him to the mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，遷司空，仍為都督南徐州諸軍事、征北將軍、南徐州刺史，給扶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, [Andu] was transferred to Minister of Works and still made Director-General of all military affairs in Southern Xuzhou, General Who Campaigns North, and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, with staff of honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Andu was made minister of works and still director-general of all military affairs in Southern Xuzhou, general who campaigns north, and Southern Xuzhou inspector, with an honorary staff.

sentences.zh: 仍別奉中旨，迎衡陽獻王昌。

translations.literal: He still separately received a secret imperial order to welcome Xian, Prince of Hengyang, Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He also received a separate secret order to welcome Xian, Prince of Hengyang, Chang.

sentences.zh: 初，昌之將入也，致書於世祖，辭甚不遜，世祖不懌，乃召安都從容而言曰：「太子將至，須別求一蕃，吾其老焉。

translations.literal: Initially, when Chang was about to enter, he sent a letter to Emperor Wen with language very lacking in deference; Emperor Wen was displeased and thus summoned Andu to speak at ease, saying: "The crown prince is about to arrive; we must seek another fief elsewhere—I am getting old."
translations.idiomatic: When Chang was about to return, he wrote to Emperor Wen in very insolent terms; the emperor was displeased and summoned Andu to speak privately: "The crown prince is coming; I must find another domain to retire to—I am growing old."

sentences.zh: 」安都對曰：「自古豈有被代天子？

translations.literal: Andu replied: "Since antiquity has there ever been a Son of Heaven who was replaced?
translations.idiomatic: Andu answered: "Has there ever been a Son of Heaven who was replaced?

sentences.zh: 臣愚不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and dares not receive such an order."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is too dull to obey such an order."

sentences.zh: 」因請自迎昌，昌濟漢而薨。

translations.literal: He thereupon asked to go himself to welcome Chang; Chang crossed the Han and died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to go welcome Chang himself; Chang crossed the Han and died on the way.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵清遠郡公，邑四千戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qingyuan commandery, fief four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was advanced to duke of Qingyuan commandery with a fief of four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 自是威名甚重，戝臣無出其右。

translations.literal: From this his martial fame was very heavy; among the great ministers none exceeded him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his prestige was immense; no minister outranked him.

sentences.zh: 安都父文捍，為始興內史，卒於官。

translations.literal: Andu's father Wenhan was Administrator of Shixing interior; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Andu's father Wenhan was administrator of Shixing interior and died in office.

sentences.zh: 世祖徵安都還京師，為發喪。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen summoned Andu back to the capital to hold mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen recalled Andu to the capital to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 尋起復本官，贈其父散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，拜其母為清遠國太夫人。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to his former office; his father was posthumously given Gentleman at the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Master of the Household with the Golden Sigil and Purple Tassel; his mother was invested as Grand Lady of Qingyuan state.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to his former post; his father was posthumously made gentleman at the imperial secretariat and grand master of the household with the golden sigil and purple tassel; his mother was made grand lady of Qingyuan state.

sentences.zh: 仍迎還都，母固求停鄉里，上乃下詔，改桂陽之汝城縣為

translations.literal: He still welcomed [her] back to the capital; his mother firmly asked to remain in the countryside; the sovereign then issued an edict, changing Guiyang's Rucheng county into
translations.idiomatic: He still brought her toward the capital; his mother insisted on staying in her home district; the court then decreed that Rucheng county in Guiyang be made

translations.literal: (lu)
translations.idiomatic: (lu)

sentences.zh: [盧]陽郡，[17]分衡州之始興、安遠二郡，合三郡為東衡州，以安都從弟曉為刺史，安都第三子祕年九歲，上以為始興內史，並令在鄉侍養。

translations.literal: [Lu]yang commandery, [17] dividing Hengzhou's Shixing and Anyuan two commanderies, combining three commanderies into Eastern Hengzhou, with Andu's younger cousin Xiao as inspector; Andu's third son Mi at nine years of age the sovereign made Administrator of Shixing interior, and ordered both to remain in the countryside to attend and support [her].
translations.idiomatic: [Lu]yang commandery, [17] taking Shixing and Anyuan from Hengzhou and combining three commanderies into Eastern Hengzhou with Andu's cousin Xiao as inspector; Andu's third son Mi, nine years old, was made administrator of Shixing interior, and both were ordered to stay home and serve her.

sentences.zh: 其年，改封安都桂陽郡公。

translations.literal: That year, [Andu's] enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Guiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That year Andu's title was changed to duke of Guiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 王琳敗後，周兵入據巴、湘，安都奉詔西討。

translations.literal: After Wang Lin's defeat, Zhou armies entered and held Ba and Xiang; Andu received orders for a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin's defeat Northern Zhou troops held Ba and Xiang; Andu was ordered west against them.

sentences.zh: 及留異擁據東陽，又奉詔東討。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi held Dongyang in rebellion, he again received orders for an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi rebelled and held Dongyang, he was ordered east again.

sentences.zh: 異本謂臺軍由錢塘江而上，安都乃步由會稽之諸暨，出于永康。

translations.literal: Yi had expected the court army to come up the Qiantang River; Andu instead marched overland through Zhuji in Kuaiji and emerged at Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi expected the imperial army up the Qiantang; Andu marched overland through Zhuji in Kuaiji and came out at Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 異大恐，奔桃枝嶺，處嶺谷間，於巖口豎柵，以拒王師。

translations.literal: Yi was greatly afraid, fled to Taozhi Ridge, and lodged in a mountain ravine; at the mouth of the gorge he set palisades to resist the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was terrified, fled to Taozhi Ridge, and camped in the ravines; at the pass he built palisades against the imperial force.

sentences.zh: 安都作連城

translations.literal: Andu built linked ramparts
translations.idiomatic: Andu built linked ramparts

translations.literal: (shou)
translations.idiomatic: (shou)

sentences.zh: [攻]異，[18]躬自接戰，為流矢所中，血流至踝，安都乘轝麾軍，容止不變。

translations.literal: [to attack] Yi, [18] personally joining battle; he was struck by a stray arrow and blood ran to his ankles; Andu rode in a litter to command the army, his bearing unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: [to attack] Yi, [18] fighting in person; a stray arrow struck him and blood ran to his ankles; Andu directed the army from a litter without changing countenance.

sentences.zh: 因其山诮之勢，迮而為堰。

translations.literal: Using the steep mountain terrain, he dammed and penned the waters.
translations.idiomatic: Using the steep mountain terrain, he dammed the stream.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年夏，潦，水漲滿，安都引船入堰，起樓艦與異城等，放拍碎其樓雉。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Tianjia, floods filled the dam; Andu brought boats into the barrier, raised tower ships level with Yi's wall, and smashed his parapets with rams.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of Tianjia year 3 the dam filled; Andu brought ships in, raised tower ships level with Yi's wall, and smashed the parapets with rams.

sentences.zh: 異與第二子忠臣脫身奔晉安，安都虜其妻子，盡收其人馬甲仗，振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Yi and his second son Zhongchen escaped to Jin'an; Andu captured his wife and children, seized all his men, horses, armor, and weapons, and returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his second son Zhongchen fled to Jin'an; Andu took their families, seized men, horses, arms, and armor, and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 以功加侍中、征北大將軍，增邑赠前五千戶，仍還本鎮。

translations.literal: For merit he was given Palace Attendant and General Who Campaigns North, his fief increased by the former five thousand households, and he returned to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made palace attendant and general who campaigns north, his fief was increased by five thousand households in all, and he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 其年，

translations.literal: That year,
translations.idiomatic: That year,

translations.literal: (shi)
translations.idiomatic: (shi)

sentences.zh: [吏]民詣闕表請立碑，[19]頌美安都功績，詔許之。

translations.literal: [Officials] and people came to court with a memorial requesting a stele, [19] praising Andu's achievements; the edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: [Officials] and commoners petitioned the throne for a stele, [19] praising Andu's deeds; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 自王琳平後，安都勳庸轉大，又自以功安社稷，漸用驕矜，數招聚文武之士，或射馭馳騁，或命以詩賦，第其高下，以差次賞賜之。
