translations.literal: After Wang Lin was pacified, Andu's achievements grew ever greater; he also considered his merit had settled the altars, and gradually grew proud and arrogant, repeatedly gathering civil and military men—some to shoot, drive, and race, others ordered to compose poetry; he ranked them high and low and rewarded them in order.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin's fall Andu's merit grew; thinking he had secured the throne, he grew proud, gathered scholars and soldiers—some for archery and racing, others for verse—and ranked them for graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 文士則褚

translations.literal: Among literary men were Chu
translations.idiomatic: Among scholars were Chu

translations.literal: (jie)
translations.idiomatic: (jie)

sentences.zh: [玠]、[20]馬樞、陰鏗、張正見、徐伯陽，劉刪、[21]祖孫登，武士則蕭摩訶、裴子烈等，並為之賓客，齋內動至千人。

translations.literal: [Jie], [20] Ma Shu, Yin Keng, Zhang Zhengjian, Xu Boyang, Liu Shan, [21] Zu Sun Deng; among warriors Xiao Mohe, Pei Zilie, and others—all became his retainers, and within his residence there were often as many as a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: [Jie], [20] Ma Shu, Yin Keng, Zhang Zhengjian, Xu Boyang, Liu Shan, [21] and Zu Sun Deng; among warriors Xiao Mohe, Pei Zilie, and others—all were his guests, and his household often held a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 部下將帥，多不遵法度，檢問收攝，則奔歸安都。

translations.literal: His subordinate commanders often did not obey the law; when investigated and arrested, they fled back to Andu.
translations.idiomatic: His officers often broke the law; when the authorities investigated, they fled to Andu.

sentences.zh: 世祖性嚴察，深銜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was by nature strict and observant and deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was strict by nature and deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 安都弗之改，日益驕橫。

translations.literal: Andu did not reform; day by day he grew more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Andu did not change and grew daily more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 每有表啟，封訖，有事未盡，乃開封自書之，云又啟某事。

translations.literal: Whenever he had a memorial, after sealing it, if something remained unsaid, he would open the seal and write himself, saying he also memorialized on such-and-such a matter.
translations.idiomatic: When he sealed a memorial but still had more to say, he opened the seal and added lines himself, noting another petition on such-and-such.

sentences.zh: 及侍讌酒酣，或箕踞傾倚。

translations.literal: When attending banquets and drunk, he would sit with legs sprawled or lean recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: At court feasts, drunk, he would sit sprawled or lean disrespectfully.

sentences.zh: 嘗陪樂遊禊飲，乃白帝曰：「何如作臨川王時？

translations.literal: Once at the Music Garden spring purification feast he said to the emperor: "How does this compare with being Prince of Linchuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Music Garden spring rites he asked the emperor: "How is this compared with your days as Prince of Linchuan?"

sentences.zh: 」帝不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not answer.

sentences.zh: 安都再三言之，帝曰：「此雖天命，抑亦明公之力。

translations.literal: Andu spoke of it again and again; the emperor said: "Though this is heaven's mandate, it is also your lordship's strength."
translations.idiomatic: Andu pressed the point; the emperor said: "Though heaven willed it, it was also your excellence."

sentences.zh: 」宴訖，又啟便借供帳水飾，將載妻妾於御堂歡會，世祖雖許其請，甚不懌。

translations.literal: When the feast ended he again memorialized to borrow furnishings and aquatic decorations, intending to bring his wives and concubines to revel in the imperial hall; Emperor Wen though he granted the request was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After the feast he asked to borrow hangings and water ornaments to bring his wives to feast in the imperial hall; Emperor Wen consented but was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 明日，安都坐於御坐，賓客居戝臣位，稱觴上壽。

translations.literal: The next day Andu sat on the imperial seat while his guests occupied the ministers' places, raising cups to offer longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Andu sat on the throne while guests took the ministers' seats and toasted the emperor.

sentences.zh: 初，重雲殿災，安都率將士帶甲入殿，帝甚惡之，自是陰為之備。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chongyun Hall burned, Andu led armored soldiers into the hall; the emperor greatly detested this and from then secretly made preparations against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyun Hall burned, Andu had led armored troops inside; the emperor hated it and thereafter quietly prepared against him.

sentences.zh: 又周迪之反，朝望當使安都討之，帝乃使吳明徹討迪，又頻遣臺使案問安都部下，檢括亡叛，安都內不自安。

translations.literal: Again when Zhou Di rebelled, the court expected Andu to be sent against him; the emperor instead sent Wu Mingche, and repeatedly dispatched court envoys to investigate Andu's subordinates and search out deserters; Andu was inwardly uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di rebelled the court had expected Andu to suppress him; the emperor sent Wu Mingche instead and repeatedly sent envoys to probe Andu's men and hunt deserters; Andu grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，遣其別駕周弘實自託於舍人蔡景歷，赠問省中事。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year he sent his aide Zhou Hongshi to entrust himself to Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Jingli, presenting gifts and inquiring into affairs within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year 3 he sent aide Zhou Hongshi to attendant Cai Jingli with gifts, asking about palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 景歷錄其狀具奏之，希旨稱安都謀反。

translations.literal: Jingli recorded the circumstances and memorialized in full, to the sovereign's intent calling Andu a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli recorded everything and memorialized, as the emperor wished, calling Andu a traitor.

sentences.zh: 世祖慮其不受制，明年春，乃除安都為都督江吳二州諸軍事、征南大將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen feared he would not submit to control; in spring of the next year he removed Andu to be Director-General of all military affairs in Jiang and Wu, General Who Campaigns South, and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would not submit, the next spring the emperor transferred Andu to director-general of all military affairs in Jiang and Wu, general who campaigns south, and Jiangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 自京口還都，部伍入于石頭，世祖引安都醼於嘉德殿，又集其部下將帥會于尚書朝堂，於坐收安都，囚于嘉德西省，又收其將帥，盡奪馬仗而釋之。

translations.literal: Returning from Jingkou to the capital, his troops entered Shitou; Emperor Wen entertained Andu at Jiade Hall and also gathered his commanders at the Masters of Writing court; at the feast he seized Andu and imprisoned him in the west wing of Jiade, seized his commanders, stripped all horses and arms, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Coming from Jingkou his troops entered Shitou; Emperor Wen feasted him at Jiade Hall and assembled his officers at the Masters of Writing court; there he seized Andu and held him in Jiade's west wing, seized his officers, took horses and weapons, and let them go.

sentences.zh: 因出舍人蔡景歷表以示於朝。

translations.literal: He then produced Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Jingli's memorial to show the court.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced attendant Cai Jingli's memorial for the court to see.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：「昔漢厚功臣，韓、彭肇亂，晉倚蕃牧，敦、約稱兵。

translations.literal: An edict then said: "In olden Han they richly rewarded merit-holders, yet Han Xin and Peng Yue raised rebellion; Jin relied on frontier governors, yet Wang Dun and Su Jun took up arms.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Han richly rewarded its merit-holders, yet Han Xin and Peng Yue rebelled; Jin relied on frontier lords, yet Wang Dun and Su Jun took arms.

sentences.zh: 託六尺於龐萌，野心竊發；

translations.literal: Entrusting a six-foot boy to Pang Meng, treacherous ambition stole forth;
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting a child to Pang Meng, treachery stirred;

sentences.zh: 寄股肱於霍禹，凶謀潛構。

translations.literal: committing the arms and legs to Huo Yu, wicked designs were secretly framed.
translations.idiomatic: committing the realm to Huo Yu, conspiracy was secretly laid.

sentences.zh: 追惟往代，挻逆一揆，永言自古，患難同規。

translations.literal: Looking back at former ages, rebellion follows one pattern; speaking forever of antiquity, disaster shares one rule.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back, rebellion repeats one pattern; through all antiquity, ruin follows one rule.

sentences.zh: 侯安都素乏遙圖，本畕令德，幸屬興運，預奉經綸，拔跡行間，假之毛羽，推於偏帥，委以馳逐。

translations.literal: Hou Andu from the first lacked far-reaching design and originally lacked fine virtue; by fortune he met a rising age and took part in state planning, plucked from the ranks and given wings, promoted from a partial commander and entrusted with pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu never had far sight and lacked virtue from the start; he met a rising age, took part in founding the state, was raised from the ranks and given rank, and as a subordinate commander was trusted with campaigns.

sentences.zh: 位極三槐，任居四嶽，名器隆赫，禮數莫儔。

translations.literal: His rank reached the three Huai trees, his office the four peaks; his titles were lofty and brilliant, his ritual unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: His rank reached the highest ministers, his post the greatest commands; his honors were dazzling and his ceremony unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 而志唯矜己，氣在陵上，招聚逋逃，窮極輕狡，無賴無行，不畏不恭。

translations.literal: Yet his will was only to exalt himself, his spirit bent on lording it over others; he gathered fugitives and exhausted every sort of knavery—unprincipled, without conduct, unafraid and without respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he thought only of himself, his temper overbearing; he gathered fugitives and every sort of knave—lawless, shameless, and insolent.

sentences.zh: 受脤專征，剽掠一逞，推轂所鎮，裒歛無厭。

translations.literal: Receiving the war tally for sole command, he plundered at will; wherever the chariot hub turned, he extorted without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: With sole command he plundered at will; in every post he extorted without end.

sentences.zh: 寄以徐蕃，接鄰齊境，伛遷禁貨，鬻賣居民，

translations.literal: Entrusted with Xu and the frontier, bordering Qi territory, he bent to traffic in forbidden goods and sold out the people,
translations.idiomatic: Posted on the Xu frontier beside Qi, he trafficked in contraband and sold out the people,

translations.idiomatic: (tui)

translations.literal: [secretly] burying and digging up [graves], [22] poison flowing through springs and soil, grudge-bearing even against corpses, heedless of law and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: [secretly] burying loot and digging graves, [22] poison seeping into earth and water, hatred even for the dead, with no regard for law.

sentences.zh: 朕以爰初締構，頗著功績，飛驂代邸，預定嘉謀，所以淹抑有司，每懷遵養，杜絕百辟，日望自新。

translations.literal: I, at the first founding, because of considerable achievement, flew my carriage to the secondary palace and took part in the good plan; therefore I restrained the offices, always cherishing forbearance, shut out the hundred officials, and daily hoped for self-renewal.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding I credited his considerable service and his part in the succession plan; I restrained the offices, always hoping he would reform, kept the court from pressing him, and daily looked for renewal.

sentences.zh: 缠襟期於話言，推丹赤於造次，策馬甲第，羽林息警，置酒高堂，陛戟無纫。

translations.literal: I opened my breast in conversation and showed my loyal heart in haste; he rode to his great mansion while the guard stood down, feasted in the high hall while halberds at the steps were unbladed.
translations.idiomatic: I spoke to him openly and showed trust in haste; he rode to his mansion while the guard stood down, feasted in the high hall while halberds at the steps were sheathed.

sentences.zh: 何嘗內隱片嫌，去柏人而勿宿，外協猜防，入成奛而不留？

translations.literal: When did I harbor the least suspicion within, dismiss the cypress guard and refuse him lodging, or outwardly feign trust yet on entering the side gate not detain him?
translations.idiomatic: When did I harbor suspicion within, refuse him lodging, or outwardly feign trust while barring him at the gate?

sentences.zh: 而勃戾不悛，驕暴滋甚，招誘文武，密懷異圖。

translations.literal: Yet he was obstinate and would not repent, arrogant and violent ever more; he enticed civil and military men and secretly harbored alien designs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he would not repent and grew ever more violent; he drew in civil and military men and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 去年十二月十一日，獲中書舍人蔡景歷啟，稱侯安都去月十日遣別駕周弘實來景歷私省宿，訪問禁中，具陳反計，朕猶加隱忍，待之如初。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the twelfth month of last year I received Palace Attendant Cai Jingli's memorial saying that on the tenth of last month Hou Andu sent his aide Zhou Hongshi to lodge privately with Jingli, inquiring into the forbidden precinct and fully stating a rebel plan; I still showed forbearance and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh of the twelfth month last year I received attendant Cai Jingli's memorial: on the tenth of last month Hou Andu sent aide Zhou Hongshi to stay privately with Jingli, asking about the inner palace and laying out a plot; I still bore with him and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 爰自北門，遷授南服，受命經停，姦謀益露。

translations.literal: From the northern gate he was transferred to southern service; during the interval of receiving orders his treacherous design grew ever clearer.
translations.idiomatic: From the northern command he was sent south; while taking up the new post his plot grew clearer.

sentences.zh: 今者欲因初鎮，將行不軌。

translations.literal: Now he wished to use his first posting to carry out unrighteous acts.
translations.idiomatic: Now he meant to use his return to command to carry out treason.

sentences.zh: 此而可忍，孰不可容？

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be borne?
translations.idiomatic: If this can be tolerated, what cannot?

sentences.zh: 賴社稷之靈，近侍誠槛，醜情彰暴，逆節顯聞。

translations.literal: Relying on the altars' spirits, loyal attendants at the bars, his ugly conduct was exposed and his rebellious intent made known.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to the state's fortune and loyal attendants at hand, his guilt was exposed and treason revealed.

sentences.zh: 外可詳案舊典，速正刑書，止在同謀，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Without, let the old statutes be consulted in detail and punishment swiftly set down in the law books; only fellow conspirators [are involved], and nothing further is to be asked.
translations.idiomatic: Let the statutes be applied and sentence passed swiftly; only fellow conspirators are implicated—no wider inquiry.

sentences.zh: 」明日，於西省賜死，時年四十四。

translations.literal: "The next day he was granted death in the west wing; he was forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was granted death in the west wing, aged forty-four.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔，宥其妻子家口，葬以士禮，喪事所須，務加資給。

translations.literal: Soon an edict pardoned his wife, children, and household; he was buried with the rites of a gentleman, and all funeral needs were to be generously supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict spared his wife, children, and household; he was buried with a gentleman's rites and funeral costs were generously provided.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖在京城，嘗與諸將醼，杜僧明、周文育、侯安都為壽，各稱功伐。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founder was in the capital, he once feasted with the generals; Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, and Hou Andu offered toasts, each boasting of his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital the Founder feasted his generals; Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, and Hou Andu toasted, each praising his deeds.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿等悉良將也，而嵭有所短。

translations.literal: The Founder said: "You are all fine generals, yet each also has shortcomings."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said: "You are all fine generals, yet each has his flaw."

sentences.zh: 杜公志大而識闇，狎於下而驕於尊，矜其功不收其拙。

translations.literal: Master Du is great in aim but dim in judgment, familiar with those below yet arrogant toward superiors, proud of his merit and not gathering in his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Master Du aims high but sees poorly, is easy with inferiors yet proud toward superiors, and boasts of merit without mending faults.

sentences.zh: 周侯交不擇人，而推心過差，居危履險，猜防不設。

translations.literal: Lord Zhou does not choose his associates yet trusts too far, treads danger without setting guards.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Zhou does not choose friends yet trusts too deeply, faces danger without precaution.

sentences.zh: 侯郎馐誕而無铬，輕佻而肆志。

translations.literal: Lord Hou is frivolous and unrestrained, light and heedless in will.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Hou is frivolous and unrestrained, light-minded and heedless.

sentences.zh: 嵭非全身之道。

translations.literal: These are not ways to preserve the whole person."
translations.idiomatic: None of these is a way to keep oneself whole."

sentences.zh: 」卒皆如其言。

translations.literal: In the end all were as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end all proved as he had said.

sentences.zh: 安都長子敦，年十二，為員外散騎侍郎，天嘉二年墮馬卒，追諡桂陽國愍世子。

translations.literal: Andu's eldest son Dun, twelve years old, was Gentleman at the Imperial Secretariat in Extraordinary Capacity; in the second year of Tianjia he fell from a horse and died, posthumously titled Lamented Heir of Guiyang state.
translations.idiomatic: Andu's eldest son Dun, twelve, was extraordinary gentleman at the imperial secretariat; in Tianjia year 2 he fell from a horse and died, posthumously titled lamented heir of Guiyang state.

sentences.zh: 太建三年，高宗追封安都為陳集縣侯，邑五百戶，子亶為嗣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taijian, Emperor Xuan posthumously enfeoffed Andu as Marquis of Chenji county, fief five hundred households, with his son Dan as heir.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 3 Emperor Xuan posthumously enfeoffed Andu as marquis of Chenji county, fief five hundred households, with son Dan as heir.

sentences.zh: 安都從弟曉，累從安都征討有功，官至員外散騎常侍、明威將軍、東衡州刺史，懷化縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Andu's younger cousin Xiao had repeatedly followed Andu on campaigns with merit, reaching Gentleman at the Imperial Secretariat in Extraordinary Capacity, General of Illustrious Might, Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, and Marquis of Huaihua county, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Andu's cousin Xiao campaigned with him many times with merit, reaching extraordinary gentleman at the imperial secretariat, general of illustrious might, Eastern Hengzhou inspector, and marquis of Huaihua county with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjia he died, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 3 he died, aged forty-one.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：杜僧明、周文育嵭樹功業，成於興運，頗、牧、韓、彭，足可連類矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Du Sengming and Zhou Wenyu alike raised achievement and stood with the rising fortune; with Fan, Mu, Han, and Peng they may well be classed together.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Du Sengming and Zhou Wenyu built their achievements in a rising age; they may be classed with Fan, Mu, Han, and Peng.

sentences.zh: 侯安都情異向時，權踰曩日，因之以侵暴，加之以縱誕，苟曰非夫逆亂，奚用免於亡滅！

translations.literal: Hou Andu's disposition differed from those of his time, his power exceeding days past; to this he added violence, and to that wantonness—if one says he was not a rebel, why should he have escaped destruction!
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu's temper differed from his peers and his power exceeded earlier days; add violence and wantonness—if he was no traitor, why escape ruin?

sentences.zh: 昔漢高醢之為賜，宋武拉於坐右，良有以而然也。

translations.literal: In olden Han Gaozu made minced meat a gift; in Song Emperor Wu dragged [a man] from his seat at the right—there was good reason for each.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu made minced meat a gift; Song's Emperor Wu dragged a man from his seat—each had its reason.
